summary: Shrank the Valdez Signal Station in Alaska to 22,946 square feet, amending a March 10, 1903, order, and reserved the adjoining lands for the War and Justice Departments.
Closed the land office at Prescott in the Arizona Land District and moved its business to Phoenix.
Gave the Spanish Treaty Claims Commission until March 2, 1905, to finish its work.
Allowed James E. S. Kinsella to be appointed a minor under instruction in the ordnance department of the Washington, D.C., navy yard without meeting Navy Yard Order No. 13.
Let Ludwick C. Young, a laborer in the Census Office, be promoted to clerk without examination, in view of his earlier service as a clerk there.
Created the Whipple Barracks Target Range Military Reservation, 1,680 acres in Yavapai County, Arizona Territory.

places.name: Whipple Barracks Target Range Military Reservation

summary: Permitted Dr. William Conyngton to be permanently appointed physician at the Grand River Indian School in North Dakota after a special examination, needed because illness at the school was rising and every eligible candidate had declined.
Amended the March 25, 1904, order concerning the Sangley Point Military Reservation.
Established the Breton Island reservation for wildlife in St. Bernard and Plaquemines Parishes, Louisiana.

Announced the death of Postmaster General Henry Clay Payne, closed the departments in Washington on the morning of his funeral, and ordered flags on public buildings nationwide flown at half-mast until he was buried.
Returned a four-acre lot in Woodward, Oklahoma Territory, once held as a county courthouse site, to the public domain so it could go to the Town of Woodward for a public park.
Set apart Thursday, November 24, 1904, as a national day of thanksgiving for a year of peace, abundant harvests and prosperity.
Allowed Luther Conant, Jr., to be appointed a special examiner in the Bureau of Corporations, at $2,500 a year, without a civil-service examination.
Reserved military land in the Philippines at Jolo (about 339.7 acres), Daraga's Regan Barracks (about 318.8 acres) and Augur Barracks, including Asturias (about 535.7 acres).

Exempted top Isthmian Canal Commission posts from civil-service examination, among them its secretary, treasurer, auditor, chief engineer, the Canal Zone governor's executive secretary, and sanitary, hospital and quarantine officers.

Brought the Isthmian Canal Commission under the civil-service act and rules, so that most officers and employees, apart from laborers, Senate-confirmed officials and detailed Army engineers, must pass an examination before being hired or promoted.

Set rules for hiring unskilled laborers in the departments at Washington, with a labor employment board under the Civil Service Commission rating applicants on physical fitness for manual work as judged by federal physicians.
Allowed Clare A. Cooper to be permanently appointed matron in the Immigration Service without examination.
Returned several Customs Service posts, including deputy or assistant collector, deputy naval officer, deputy surveyor and cashier, to the competitive service, so they now require examination.
Created the Warner Mountains Forest Reserve in California, closing the timbered public lands within its boundaries to entry and settlement.
Established the Modoc Forest Reserve in northern California along the state line, reserving its partly timbered public lands from entry and settlement.
Classified substitute watchmen at the Government Printing Office under the civil-service rules, including the forty men already serving on the Public Printer's list.

Barred executive departments from hiring anyone to do the work of classified employees except under the civil-service rules, and sent doubtful cases to the Civil Service Commission and, failing agreement, to the Attorney General.
Allowed James Rankin Young of Pennsylvania to be appointed Superintendent of the Dead Letter Office without examination.
Allowed Marcus Braun to be permanently appointed an immigrant inspector in the Immigration Service without examination.
Permitted Capt. Joseph Watkinson to be permanently appointed assistant inspector of hulls in the Steamboat Inspection Service without examination.
Reduced the South Platte Forest Reserve in Colorado, releasing some lands back to the public domain for later settlement while keeping the rest reserved.
Enlarged the Camp Eldridge Military Reservation at Los Baños, Luzon, listed at 68.35 acres, modifying an order of September 1, 1903.
Allowed the U.S. citizenship requirement to be waived for applicants for jobs on the Isthmus of Panama, under Civil Service Commission regulations.
Allowed Mrs. William H. Tabberah to be permanently appointed keeper of the Cumberland Head Light Station in New York without examination.

Set rules for hiring unskilled laborers in federal offices outside Washington, starting in New York, Boston, Philadelphia and St. Louis, with local civil-service boards registering applicants aged 20 to 60.

Placed the General Land Office employees who protect and administer the forest reserves, in the field and in Washington, under the civil-service rules, so new hires and promotions require examination.
Redrew the boundaries of the Big Horn Forest Reserve in Wyoming, setting a date for excluded lands to open to settlement.
Exempted from examination a consulting architect hired by the War Department to rebuild the U.S. Military Academy at West Point, New York.
Authorized permanent appointments for thirteen clerks in the Bureau of the Census.
Forbade federal employees who are also notaries public from charging fees for notarial acts done for the government, its workers in their official roles, or anyone during office hours.
Added more Canal Zone posts to the list exempt from civil-service examination, including judges, court officers, mayors, police and locally hired skilled tradesmen earning $4 a day or less.
Classified the Washington department laborers who had been doing clerical-grade work since 1902, allowing them to be promoted to clerk or transferred under the civil-service rules.
Named Joseph L. Bristow special commissioner to look into trade and freight rates across the Isthmus of Panama and the management of the Panama Railroad.
Established Camp Marahui Military Reservation, later called Camp Keithley, in Moro Province on Mindanao in the Philippines.
Removed Alaska's Customs Service from the blanket civil-service exemption for hard-to-fill Alaska posts, while exempting seasonal Alaska customs workers hired only for the navigation season.
Extended the deadline for the Spanish Treaty Claims Commission to finish its work to September 2, 1905.
Allowed Stephen W. Fuller, a messenger boy at the Library of Congress, to transfer to messenger in the Bureau of Manufactures, Department of Commerce and Labor.
Moved the duties, records and files of the Commissioner of Railroads from the Interior Department to the Department of Commerce and Labor.
Allowed the U.S. citizenship requirement to be waived for applicants seeking officer posts on Coast and Geodetic Survey ships serving in the Philippine Islands.
Allowed George F. Otis to be reinstated as a clerk in the Quartermaster's Department despite the one-year limit on reinstatement.
Called the U.S. Senate into special session at the Capitol at noon on March 4, 1905, to receive communications from the President.
Formed a commission to investigate how aliens are naturalized under existing law, with its findings due by November 15, 1905.
Allowed John Nolan to be reinstated as a Postal Service carrier without regard to civil-service time limits.
Ended the examination exemption for Interior Department special agents protecting public lands and for inspectors of surveyors-general and district land offices.
Exempted from examination five General Land Office special agents assigned to investigate fraudulent land entries and other criminal matters.
Exempted from examination Indian Service physicians paid no more than $720 a year who may also keep a private practice, with each hire subject to Commission approval.

Allowed retired Army officers to be appointed Indian school superintendents without competitive examination, at the request of the Commissioner of Indian Affairs and with the Interior Secretary's approval.
Set aside the Stump Lake Reservation in North Dakota as a preserve and breeding ground for birds.
Let Donald G. Mitchell, Jr., who had supervised construction of the Government Hospital for the Insane's new buildings, stay on as supervisor of buildings and grounds without examination.
Enlarged the lands set apart for the Navajo Indian Reservation in Utah.
Waived civil-service rules so Mrs. Catharine M. Gallagher, who left an Interior Department clerkship in 1901, could be reinstated in a Washington department at no higher grade.
Barred laborers classified as clerks from further pay raises unless they pass the examination for promotion to the clerical grade.
Allowed Dr. Cyrus Adler to be appointed assistant secretary in charge of the library and exchanges at the Smithsonian Institution, at $2,700 a year, without examination.

Created an unpaid consultative board of architects, chaired by Bernard R. Green, that must review the site and exterior design of every new public building in the District of Columbia before approval.
Allowed Sydnie Kennedy to be appointed chief of division, clerk and stenographer in the Isthmian Canal Service, at $1,800 a year, without examination.
Allowed W. G. Tucker to be appointed a clerk with the Isthmian Canal Commission, at $1,500 a year, without examination.
Allowed Mrs. M. G. Lauxmann to be permanently appointed a writer in the Coast and Geodetic Survey without examination.
Set the compensation for the consultative board of architects.
Created the Pinal Mountains Forest Reserve in Arizona Territory, reserving its partly timbered public lands from entry and settlement.
Moved the land office at Oregon City to Portland.
Approved the Secretary of War's recommendation to reserve certain lands in Minnesota for flowage purposes.
Established the Plumas Forest Reserve in California, setting its partly timbered public lands apart from entry and settlement.
Revoked Executive Order 310, which had set the compensation of the consultative board of architects.
Changed the boundaries of the Madison Forest Reserve in Montana, releasing some lands and opening them to settlement.
Allowed George W. Pitts, a skilled laborer at Commerce and Labor, to be appointed messenger in the Post Office Department without the usual six months of prior service.

Proclaimed an international naval, marine and military celebration on Hampton Roads, Virginia, from May 13 to November 1, 1907, marking 300 years since the Jamestown settlement, and invited foreign nations to send ships and troops.
Transferred certain lands from the Lakeview Land District in Oregon to the Burns Land District.
Ended the examination exemption for Post Office Department cashiers and finance clerks, denying those already appointed competitive status unless the Postmaster General recommends it.
Classified laborers assigned to clerical-grade work since the January 1905 order and forbade any further such assignments; laborers needed for that work must now come from civil-service registers.
Extended the November 1904 order classifying substitute watchmen at the Government Printing Office to five more men hired after the original list.
Exempted from examination the Reclamation Service's consulting engineers and a confidential clerk and record clerk for the superintendent of the Government Hospital for the Insane.
Allowed S. F. Scott, Jr., to be reinstated in the Post Office Service despite the time limit on reinstatement.
Revoked the February 9, 1905, order that had moved the Commissioner of Railroads' office to the Department of Commerce and Labor.
Required civil-service examination for Bureau of Immigration employees working in countries bordering the United States, narrowing an exemption for federal jobs abroad.
Amended the December 1904 notary-fee ban so it no longer covers oaths of disinterestedness and other oaths required by law, as long as the work is done outside office hours.
Reorganized the Isthmian Canal Commission.
Created the Trinity Forest Reserve in California, reserving its partly timbered public lands from entry and settlement.
Amended the civil-service rules to exempt certain War Department firemen from examination.
Let the Navy Department discharge, on request, men of the messmen branch who enlist for the Naval Academy midshipmen's summer practice cruise, modifying an order of August 13, 1902.
Allowed Edward H. Hareford to be transferred to forest assistant in the Department of Agriculture without regard to civil-service rules.
Abolished the Ironton Land District in Missouri and folded it into the Springfield Land District.
Approved the Secretary of War's recommendation to reserve lands around Subic Bay, Luzon, in the Philippine Islands for military purposes.
Abolished the Marysville Land District and transferred its business to the Sacramento Land District.
Abolished the Boonville Land District and moved it into the Springfield Land District.
Established the Uintah Land District.
Established the Klamath Forest Reserve in northern California, reserving its partly timbered public lands from entry and settlement.
Withdrew part of the abandoned Fort Sherman Military Reservation from sale and granted it to the town of Coeur d'Alene, Idaho, for a public cemetery, as the townspeople had petitioned.
Created the Wallowa Forest Reserve in northeastern Oregon, closing its partly timbered public lands to entry and settlement.
Added lands to the Grand Canyon Forest Reserve in Arizona Territory, which had been established in 1893.
